external.description: TNB’s Project Chlorobloom is one of the most quietly interesting climate experiments in Malaysian industrial history. It deserves far more attention than it is getting. Somewhere in Manjung, Perak, flue gas from a coal-fired power plant is being fed into tanks of green water. Inside those tanks, microscopic algae are eating the carbon dioxide, multiplying at speed, and producing biomass that could one day end up in a fish farm, a fertiliser bag, or the fuel tank of a commercial aircraft. This is not science fiction. It is Project Chlorobloom — TNB’s Biological Carbon Capture and Utilisation initiative, which channels […]
